transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you. Well, I came in because... I just keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. I notice it a lot in photos, and especially under the bright lights at the store where I work. Even when other people tell me they don't see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. It's just been really bothering me lately.
Do you find yourself frequently checking that spot in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?

Yeah, I do. On my breaks at work, I usually end up going to the bathroom just to check my face in the mirror. I'll spend time fixing my hair around it, trying to see if I can make it less noticeable. And I guess I also catch myself comparing my face to the girls who come through my checkout line. Sometimes I get so caught up looking in the mirror and messing with my hair that I take too long, and I actually end up being late getting back to the register.
Apart from your concerns about this spot on your face, do you feel anxious in social situations for other reasons, like worrying you might say or do something embarrassing?

No, not really. I don't worry about saying the wrong thing or embarrassing myself like that. I'm usually pretty okay talking to the customers and everything. It's really just... just the thing with my face that makes me uncomfortable when people are looking at me.

Besides concerns about your appearance, do you experience repetitive thoughts or routines about other things, like fears of contamination, checking locks, or needing things arranged in a specific way?
No, I don't really have anything like that. I don't worry about germs or checking the door or anything. It's really just the thing with my face that I get stuck on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (a slight uneven spot on the cheek/nose) that others do not notice. This preoccupation leads to repetitive mirror checking, grooming/concealing behaviors, and comparing appearance with others, resulting in functional impairment at work (running late to register). Social anxiety disorder and generalized obsessive-compulsive disorder were excluded.

Belief that others focus on and notice the perceived flaw
Repetitive mirror checking and appearance checking
Excessive grooming and attempts to conceal the perceived flaw
Frequent comparison of appearance with other individuals

additional_requirements: Symptoms not better explained by concerns with body fat/weight in an eating disorder
